## What it is

Komga serves your comics, manga, magazines and e-books (CBZ, CBR, PDF, EPUB) to a web reader and to reading apps through OPDS and the Kobo sync ([gotson/komga](https://github.com/gotson/komga)).

**Licence:** `MIT` (GitHub licence API). Market class **L1**. There is no license-matrix row yet, so the gate notes that it is not preinstallable on sold boxes until one is added (brief 30 B10).

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## Market listing

- Category and sub-tags (docs/design/TAXONOMY.md §1): media: books. The sub-tags go into `metadata.tags` once the schema has it.
- Deployment class (TAXONOMY §2): **Market · community** until CI writes a passing scan (contract §9.4), then Market · verified if every check passes.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment` (`Recreate`), one container (Java), as UID 1000. The image has no `USER` and no entrypoint script, so it runs as whatever user starts it. No privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped.
- Volumes: `komga-config` (5 GiB, `/config`) and `komga-library` (50 GiB, `/data`, for your books).
- The JVM heap may use up to 75% of the 1 GiB limit (`JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS`).
- Probes: `GET /` (the web reader).

## First run

Source: [komga.org docs](https://komga.org/docs/introduction).

1. Install Komga from the Market and approve the action. It installs into `app-komga`.
2. Forward the port and open http://localhost:25600:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-komga port-forward svc/komga 25600:25600
   ```
3. Create the admin account on the first page. Do this right after install: the first account created becomes the admin.
4. Copy books into the library volume (`/data`), then add a library pointing at `/data` (or a folder in it).

## Not done yet

- Getting books onto the library volume has no OneMind screen yet; until the Files app can write to app volumes, use `kubectl cp` or a file-sharing app.
- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: OneMind v0 has no ingress or certificates for apps, so the web UI is reached through a port-forward until the app proxy exists. Reading apps (OPDS, Kobo) need that LAN address.
- `readOnlyRootFilesystem` is not set: it has not been tested against this image.
- Resource figures are OneMind choices; upstream publishes none. They are checked against real use when the CI smoke test (contract §9.4 check 9) runs.
- `metadata.tier` stays `community` until `sdk/tools/app-gate` in CI writes a passing `scan.json`. `spec.updates.automerge` is `none` until `renovate.json` lists the app.

## Why this app is blocked

The CI app gate (`sdk/tools/app-gate`, contract §9.4) computed tier **blocked** for this app on 2026-11-12 (ci-apps run 43212771377, job `gate (komga)`). The gateway lists a blocked app in the Market but refuses to install it (§10.3, §11.1). The app is kept, not hidden, and the gate was not weakened. Reasons from that run:

- Vulnerability: `docker.io/gotson/komga:1.30.1`: CVE-2026-75595 in `io.netty:netty-handler` 4.1.135.Final (fixed 4.1.137.Final); CVE-2026-55276, CVE-2026-65182, CVE-2026-65637, CVE-2026-65905 and CVE-2026-68525 in `tomcat-embed-core` 10.1.55 (fixed 10.1.56 to 10.1.59); CVE-2026-47890 and CVE-2026-47892 in `spring-webflux` 6.2.19 and CVE-2026-47884 and CVE-2026-47890 in `spring-webmvc` 6.2.19 (fixed 7.0.9).
- Licence: GitHub MIT matches, but there is no research licence-matrix row, so the app is not preinstallable on sold boxes until one is added (brief 30 B10).
- Passed: ClamAV (0 infected), smoke test (GET / returned 200).

To unblock: move the pins to upstream releases that fix these findings (tags that exist, checked with `crane`), then rerun `sdk/tools/app-gate` (the daily `apps-rescan` workflow does this too). Nothing is bumped to an unverified tag.
